description: Calls the members of an interface on a server, from .NET or Fable: the wire format, pluggable, and the client.
releaseNotes:
### Changed
**Breaking:** the `Effect` type's static `Return` returns an effect of the type it's a member of, `Effect<'r, 'a, 'e>.Return: 'a -> Effect<'r, 'a, 'e>`, instead of being a generic method returning any effect, so code compiled against 0.8.0 that calls it must be recompiled. A second `Return` takes an effect of the type and returns a function making one, and a static `Bind` binds an effect, as `>>=` does

### Added
Fable support for JavaScript: `Effect`, `eff` and the `Effect` module, from the `Orsak` package, which carries the sources Fable compiles. Effects run on `Task`, which Fable compiles to promises, and `fanOut`, effect sequences, the base effects, resilience and scopes are .NET only, see the Fable guide (experimental)
Orsak.Remoting and Orsak.Remoting.AspNetCore: a client, compiled with Fable or on .NET, calls the members of an interface on an ASP.NET Core server, which serves them with `MapRemote`. The wire format is pluggable, `IWireFormat`, and JSON is the first, the same on .NET and Fable; the contract's errors cross as values, and a failed call raises `RemoteCallException`, see the Remoting guide (experimental)
Orsak.Myriad: `[<GenRemote>]` generates the proxy of a remote interface, which makes the codecs of each member once, so a type the format can't write fails when the proxy is made, as `MapRemote` does when it maps the endpoints (experimental)
Orsak.Remoting: a format of a self-describing encoding is `WireFormat(encoding)`, Orsak.Remoting's mapping of F# types to `WireValue`s with an `IWireEncoding` of them to bytes, a few dozen lines over a library such as MessagePack-CSharp or System.Text.Json; `Conformance` checks an encoding, and that a client's and a server's encodings agree. `JsonFormat` is the JSON encoding's, with the content type `application/vnd.orsak+json`, writes byte arrays as base64, and reads non-public types (experimental)
Orsak.Remoting: `RemoteCallException.StatusCode` is the status the server answered, such as 401 or 403, or `None` if it couldn't be reached; `FetchTransport` takes headers, asked for on each request, such as a bearer token, and fetch's credentials mode. Orsak.Remoting.AspNetCore: a member's attributes, such as `[<Authorize(Roles = "editor")>]`, are its endpoint's metadata, and arguments that can't be read are answered 400, not 500. The Remoting guide has a section on authorization (experimental)
Orsak.Remoting: enums, by name, the smaller integer types, `uint32` and `uint64`, maps, sets, `ResizeArray`, `HashSet`, `Dictionary`, `float32`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly` and `TimeSpan` cross the wire, the dates and times as ISO 8601 strings written the same on .NET and Fable, and an option of an option keeps `Some None` apart from `None` (experimental)
Orsak.Remoting: a member taking a `CancellationToken` can be cancelled. The token isn't sent: the client's aborts the request, so the call raises `OperationCanceledException`, and `MapRemote` passes the member the request's `RequestAborted` in its place. A member returning `Async` is cancelled with the `Async`. A transport's `Post` takes the token too (experimental)
Orsak.Remoting: a member returning a `RemoteStream` streams its items, which the client reads as they come, on Fable and .NET. On .NET it is an `IAsyncEnumerable`, so a server returns one, such as an effect sequence; on Fable, an interface with members of the same names. Each reading is a call, pulled item by item, and stopping it ends the call. A transport has `PostStream`, and `[<GenRemote>]` generates the proxies of stream members, see the Remoting guide (experimental)
Fable: the base effects `Time`, `GuidGenerator`, `Random` and `CancellationSource`. Fable has no `System.TimeProvider`, so an `ITimeProvider`'s clock is Orsak's own `TimeProvider` there, with `TimeProvider.System` and `GetUtcNow` as on .NET; `Time.delay` isn't ended by the environment's cancellation source on Fable. Code generated by `[<GenEffects>]` compiles with Fable, see the Fable guide (experimental)

### Fixed
`return!` of a `Task<'T>` in an `eff` returns the task's value, instead of `unit`, and can be used in a `try` block too
The `Effect` type's `<*>` applies an effect of a function to an effect of its argument, for FSharpPlus too, as up to 0.5.0. From 0.6.0 it expected the function to return the type it was applied to, so it couldn't be used
A `for` in an `effList` runs its body in a loop when the effect runs, so it can go over any number of items. It nested an effect for each item, which overflowed the stack at a few hundred, copied the list so far for each, and ran each body as the effect was built, so an error didn't stop the loop
An `effSeq` disposed before its end, as by a reader that stops early or is cancelled, runs its `finally` blocks and disposes what it `use`s, innermost first. They didn't run, so what the sequence had opened stayed open
